report:
I reproduced the bug. The cause is in `QuestionRow`, which copies each question's answer into its own local state, combined with FlashList reusing row components while you scroll. I didn't change any code. I didn't watch FlashList reuse a row directly, so that part is inferred from the code plus the on-screen evidence.

## Steps to reproduce

1. I launched `org.reactjs.native.example.RNUpgradeLab` on the iPhone 17 simulator (it was sitting on the home screen). The "Store audit" list loaded with the header "0 of 48 answered" and no pill highlighted.
2. I tapped **yes** on "Fire exit clear of obstructions", the first row. The header changed to "1 of 48 answered" and only that pill was highlighted.
3. I scrolled down in steps of about half a screen.

## Evidence

| Scroll position | What I saw |
|---|---|
| Food safety | No rows highlighted |
| Cleaning | **"Entrance mats clean" shows yes highlighted.** The header still says "1 of 48 answered" |
| Shelves and Checkouts | No rows highlighted |
| Staff | **"Break room clean" shows yes highlighted.** The header still says "1 of 48 answered" |
| Back at the top | "Fire exit clear of obstructions" is still yes and the header still says 1 |

The header count comes from the list's real answer data, which holds one answer. So the two extra "yes" pills on rows I never touched exist only on screen, not in the data. This matches what the auditor described.

## Root cause

**`src/components/QuestionRow.tsx:15`**
```tsx
const [answer, setAnswer] = useState(item.answer);
```
- Each row keeps its own copy of the answer, seeded from `item.answer` only when the row first mounts. The comment above it says this is so the pill highlights instantly.
- The pill highlight reads this local copy (`:27` and `:32`).
- Tapping a pill updates both the local copy and the parent list (`:29-30`), so the two agree for the row you tapped.
- If the row is later given a different question, React keeps the old local value and ignores the new `item.answer`.

**`src/screens/ChecklistScreen.tsx:30-34`**
- `<FlashList>` reuses row components as you scroll, to save memory.
- `getItemType={item => item.kind}` (`:33`) puts every question into one shared pool. A row that scrolls off screen is handed to a different question, as the same component instance.
- `<QuestionRow item={item} onAnswer={answer} />` (`:42`) is rendered with no `key` that would force a reset. Only the `item` prop changes.

The row that held "Fire exit…" (local state `'yes'`) scrolled off, was reused for "Entrance mats clean", and kept showing "yes". The same happened for "Break room clean". Which rows are affected depends on the order FlashList recycles them, which is why only some rows were hit.

The reverse should also happen: an answer you really gave can show as unanswered or as the wrong value after a scroll. I didn't test that case.

## Unrelated issue

`src/lib/risk.ts:13-17` builds a new regular expression 200 times per keyword for every row render. That is wasteful and could slow scrolling, but it has nothing to do with this bug.

A fix would be to take `answer` straight from `item.answer` instead of copying it into state. I haven't tried that.
